about: Emotion and sound tags Forge text can carry when it is spoken, and how each expressive voice renders them. Write a tag in square brackets anywhere in the text: '[angry] I told you to fall back. [sigh]'. Several in one bracket are fine: '[sad, whisper]'. Tags marked "round" (sounds and pauses) also work in round brackets: '(laughs)'; moods do not, so '(normal)' in a sentence is still read. Full-width brackets count: '［怒り］', '（笑）'. Bracket text that is not a known tag or alias is left alone. A voice model row opts in with "expressive": "<style>" (shared/voice_registry.json); every other model gets the tags taken out by the 'plain' style, so a plain voice never reads 'angry' aloud. The first emotion or delivery tag of a request is its mood: a cloned voice picks that clip from its profile (models/voice/profiles/<id>/), if it has one. Adding a tag or a style is an edit here only. Code: apps/voice/expressive.py.

plain.about: Every voice without an expressive style: tags come out, a pause becomes an ellipsis.

irodori.about: Irodori-TTS (Japanese): emoji in the text, placed where the tag was (the model card's table). A tag eats the space after it.

omnivoice.about: OmniVoice: its own bracket tags for sounds, in place; the mood picks the profile clip.

auk.about: AuK clones the words only; the mood picks the profile clip. edits are AuK's own instructions, used by apps/voice/profiles.py to make a profile's emotion clips from its calm clip (once, not per line).

edits.whisper: Convert this speech into a soft whisper while preserving the speaker and content.

breeze.about: Breeze TTS 2: the mood becomes the spoken-direction instruction; laughs and sighs are its own vocal tags, which need a stronger cfg_scale.

instructions.happy: Speak happily, with a smile in the voice.
instructions.angry: Speak angrily, frustrated and raising the voice.
instructions.sad: Speak sadly and quietly, close to tears.
instructions.whisper: Whisper softly, as if someone might overhear.
